high.title: Bursa ends higher on late buying interest
high.summary: The FBM KLCI closed marginally higher at 1,683.61 despite pressure from rising oil prices following US airstrikes on Iran and the revocation of Iran's oil export waiver. Late institutional buying rescued the index from session lows, signaling resilient domestic sentiment. Investors remain cautious over geopolitical risks affecting energy prices, inflation, and global interest rate outlooks.

high.title: Ringgit ends higher against major currencies but slips versus US dollar
high.summary: The ringgit weakened against the US dollar amid escalating US-Iran tensions, with Brent crude surging 5.68% to US$78.28 per barrel following US military strikes and the revocation of Iran's oil export waiver. Concerns over potential closure of the Strait of Hormuz pose significant risks to global oil supply chains. Upcoming FOMC minutes are also expected to influence currency and market direction.

high.title: S&P 500 ends down after Trump says Iran deal is over
high.summary: US equities fell after Trump declared Iran negotiations over at the NATO summit, raising fears of prolonged military conflict and potential Iranian retaliation. Major tech stocks including Microsoft, Alphabet, and Meta declined over 1-2%, signaling broad risk-off sentiment that could spill over into Asian markets including Malaysia. The geopolitical escalation adds uncertainty to global supply chains and energy markets.

high.title: Ringgit ends higher as weaker greenback, firmer oil lift sentiment
high.summary: The ringgit strengthened to 4.0685/4.0735 against the USD at close, supported by a weaker greenback and firmer oil prices. Geopolitical tensions from a US-Iran attack raised concerns over their ongoing nuclear deal negotiations. Markets await the FOMC meeting minutes for clearer Fed rate direction, with the ringgit remaining technically oversold and poised for further gains.

high.title: Ringgit slips as investors return to US dollar after weak jobs report
high.summary: The ringgit weakened to 4.0825/4.0875 against the USD as investors shifted back to the US dollar following a weak US jobs report. Caution prevailed ahead of the Fed's June meeting minutes, with Asian currencies broadly softer. The ISM services index release was a key data point being monitored by market participants.

high.title: Ringgit may rebound on capital flow measures, say analysts
high.summary: Analysts from RBC and ANZ forecast the ringgit could strengthen to RM3.95–RM3.80 per dollar by year-end, driven by BNM's intensified measures to encourage repatriation and conversion of overseas earnings. The ringgit has outperformed all Asian peers since BNM's June 24 pledge, supported by a solid trade surplus and strong foreign demand for ringgit-denominated bonds. This represents a significant policy-driven currency outlook with direct implications for investors, exporters, and importers.

high.title: Ringgit opens firmer as traders reassess US rate hike prospects
high.summary: The ringgit opened firmer at 4.0695/4.0780 against the USD as markets reassess Fed rate hike prospects following weaker US jobs data. Key upcoming events include the FOMC minutes release and BNM's MPC meeting both scheduled for Thursday, July 9, which could significantly influence monetary policy direction. These dual policy events make this a critical week for Malaysian financial markets.

high.title: Rebound in banking stocks lifts Bursa at close
high.summary: The FBM KLCI surged 17.22 points to close at 1,679.05, driven by a rebound in heavyweight banking stocks. The rally was fuelled by weaker-than-expected US non-farm payrolls of 57,000 against forecasts of 113,000, easing fears of further Fed rate hikes. This significantly improves risk appetite for Malaysian equities and reduces concerns over tighter global financial conditions.

high.title: Ringgit rises as weak US jobs data lifts rate cut hopes
high.summary: The ringgit strengthened to 4.0705/4.0805 against the USD following disappointing US nonfarm payroll data of 57,000 jobs in June, far below the 114,000 consensus forecast. The weak data reduces the likelihood of a Fed rate hike, supporting further ringgit appreciation. Technical indicators also suggest the ringgit is in oversold territory, pointing to potential near-term gains.

medium.title: Bursa opens higher, outperforms regional peers
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI opened 0.38% higher at 1,689.35, outperforming regional peers despite overnight Wall Street losses driven by AI stock selloffs and rising Middle East tensions. Brent crude rose to around US$74 per barrel following fresh attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, while the US 10-year Treasury yield edged up to 4.551%. The mixed global backdrop highlights selective resilience in the Malaysian market.

medium.title: Ringgit eases against US dollar as Middle East tensions rise
medium.summary: The ringgit opened weaker at 4.0745/4.0830 against the US dollar as global markets shifted to risk-off mode following US military strikes on Iran and the revocation of Iran's oil sales waiver. Brent crude jumped 6.13% to US$76.40 per barrel, reflecting heightened supply disruption fears. The ringgit did strengthen against other major currencies including the yen, pound, and euro.

medium.title: Bursa ends marginally lower on mild profit-taking
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI eased slightly by 0.60 points to close at 1,682.93, reflecting normal consolidation after recent gains rather than a sentiment reversal. Analysts noted the index remains supported above recent lows, with easing geopolitical tensions and moderating energy prices underpinning the market. The short-term recovery trend is considered intact.

medium.title: Bursa slips after recent gains as sellers return
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI slipped 4.01 points in early trade as sellers returned following recent gains, with market breadth slightly negative. Turnover was modest at RM54.48 million, reflecting cautious investor sentiment despite the previous session's firmer close. Rakuten Trade's Kenny Yee highlighted ongoing caution as the key market undertone.

medium.title: Ringgit opens slightly higher amid focus on Fed outlook
medium.summary: The ringgit opened marginally higher at 4.0815/4.0880 against the USD, though it weakened against most other major currencies. Fed Governor Waller's hawkish stance on inflation reinforced the higher-for-longer interest rate narrative, keeping the USD well supported. Investors remained focused on upcoming Fed guidance as the key driver for ringgit direction.

medium.title: Bursa ends higher, lifted by banking and plantation stocks
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI rose 4.48 points (0.27%) to close at 1,683.53, supported by banking and plantation stocks amid easing geopolitical tensions and declining crude oil prices. Bargain-hunting in blue-chip stocks contributed to the rebound, though market breadth remained negative with losers outpacing gainers. This reflects cautious but improving domestic investor sentiment.

medium.title: Bursa opens firmer on improved investor sentiment
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI opened 3.35 points higher at 1,682.40, buoyed by Wall Street gains and diminished US rate hike expectations following weaker-than-expected US jobs data. Rakuten Trade projects the index to trade in the 1,675–1,695 range, suggesting a stable but cautious session. The easing rate hike outlook could encourage equity inflows into Bursa.

medium.title: Ringgit closes higher on positive Asian currency sentiment
medium.summary: The ringgit appreciated to 4.0690/4.0735 against the USD on Friday, driven by weaker-than-expected US NFP data reducing pressure on the Fed to raise rates. Asian currencies broadly gained against the dollar, with the ringgit touching an intraday high of 4.0600. This positive close sets a constructive tone heading into the new trading week.

medium.title: Bursa opens higher on consumer stock gains
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI opened higher at 1,665.73, gaining 3.65 points in early trade on consumer stock gains, though market breadth was negative with losers outnumbering gainers. Mixed US equity performance overnight, with chip stock weakness offsetting cooling labour market optimism, provided a cautious backdrop. This early session data offers context for intraday trading sentiment on Bursa.

medium.title: Ringgit closes higher against greenback, regional currencies
medium.summary: The ringgit appreciated to 4.0780/4.0830 against the USD, gaining 0.33% as markets awaited the critical US Nonfarm Payrolls report. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh's data-dependent stance at the ECB Forum in Sintra added uncertainty to the rate outlook, keeping currency markets attentive. The result sets the stage for the subsequent ringgit movements reported on July 3.
